scales.name: Drive
scales.definition: Exploration plus willingness to expend effort for reward.

facets.name: Exploration
facets.definition: Seeking novelty and information without external prompting.

facets.name: Effort tolerance
facets.definition: Willingness to pay a cost for a larger reward.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Dopamine agonists can produce impulse-control disorders, and amphetamine raises willingness to expend effort for reward.
bodyLinks.verification: Not individually verifiable; the causal evidence is from drug manipulation, not from measuring a person's level.

scales.name: Unusual cognition
scales.definition: Tendency toward unusual perceptions, associations and beliefs.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Antipsychotics act by D2 blockade and amphetamine can induce psychosis, making this the dimension with the strongest dopamine evidence.
bodyLinks.verification: No individual-level test; inference is from pharmacology at the group level.

scales.name: Impairment
scales.definition: How much current functioning is affected. Crossed with every other scale to distinguish trait from problem.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Functional impact is measured directly and carries no biological claim.

scales.name: Sleep reactivity
scales.definition: How much mood, patience and initiative change after a short night.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Sleep loss degrades motivation and emotion regulation, and insomnia severity tracks depression risk.
bodyLinks.verification: Observed coupling between logged sleep and next-day state over 3+ weeks of tracking.

scales.name: Chronotype
scales.definition: Corrected mid-sleep on free days (MSFsc) as a proxy for circadian phase.

bodyLinks.mechanism: MSFsc from the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire correlates with dim-light melatonin onset at roughly r = .54-.68.
bodyLinks.verification: Wearable sleep timing across free days; DLMO in a research setting.

review.notes: Rewritten from a 'a sign was meant for me' phrasing, which indexed religiosity rather than the construct. This version asks about others' reactions to the behavior instead of the belief's content. Must be DIF-tested by religiosity before piloting.

items.informantText: In the past two weeks they have talked about hurting themselves.

flags.name: Alcohol flush response
flags.target: ALDH2 deficiency — a discrete genotype affecting alcohol metabolism

confirmationRoutes.name: Serum ferritin
confirmationRoutes.description: A routine blood test measuring iron stores.
confirmationRoutes.thresholdNote: Restless-legs research uses <50 µg/L as the relevant threshold, while lab 'normal' ranges often start at 15 — so a 'normal' result can still be relevant.
confirmationRoutes.accessNote: Ask a GP, or order through a standard lab panel where direct-access testing is available.

confirmationRoutes.name: ALDH2 genotype
confirmationRoutes.description: Reported by most consumer genetic tests, or by a clinical genetics lab.
confirmationRoutes.accessNote: An observed flush after one drink is also reasonable confirmation.

interactionRules.rationale: High drive combined with cycling energy and functional impact is the pattern with the strongest longitudinal link to bipolar-spectrum outcomes; the Hypomanic Personality Scale was the best single predictor over 23 years (d = 0.67).
High impairment without an elevated trait profile is the cell that prevents false reassurance: something is affecting this person that the profile does not explain.

citations.title: The neuromodulator of exploration: a unifying theory of the role of dopamine in personality
citations.claim: Dopamine's general function is to promote exploration, linking it to Extraversion and Openness/Intellect.

citations.title: Dopaminergic mechanisms of individual differences in human effort-based decision-making
citations.claim: Striatal and vmPFC dopamine responsivity predicts willingness to expend effort for larger rewards.

citations.title: DOMINION study: impulse control disorders in Parkinson's disease
citations.claim: Impulse control disorders occur in about 17% of Parkinson's patients taking a dopamine agonist, 2-3x the rate of those not taking one.

citations.title: PMDD symptoms following ovarian suppression: triggered by change in ovarian steroid levels but not continuous stable levels
citations.claim: Behavioral response depends on sensitivity to hormonal change rather than on hormone level.

citations.title: Concordance of chronotype categorisations based on DLMO, MEQ and MCTQ
citations.claim: MCTQ-derived MSFsc correlates with dim-light melatonin onset, supporting questionnaire measurement of circadian phase.

citations.title: Investigator-observed alcohol-induced flushing but not self-report of flushing is a valid predictor of ALDH2 genotype
citations.claim: Self-reported flushing is 100% sensitive but only 68% specific for ALDH2 genotype.

citations.title: Validation of alcohol flushing questionnaires in determining inactive ALDH2
citations.claim: Modified flushing questionnaires reach about 95% sensitivity and 77% specificity for inactive ALDH2.

citations.title: Ferric carboxymaltose in patients with restless legs syndrome and nonanemic iron deficiency: a randomized trial
citations.claim: Iron repletion improved restless legs severity in non-anemic iron deficiency.

citations.title: Predictive and discriminant validity of psychopathology and temperament scales - 23-year follow-up, Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966
citations.claim: High Hypomanic Personality Scale score was the best predictor of later bipolar disorder (d = 0.67).

citations.title: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP): a quantitative nosology based on consensus of evidence
citations.claim: Psychopathology is distributed dimensionally; no common mental disorder has been verified as a categorical entity.
